title: Repair error-budget span totals and throughput
statement_md:
# Error-budget span report

A reliability service records how many errors occurred in each minute and answers many
span queries: "how many errors happened between minute `start` and minute `end`?"
Three regressions were introduced: some span totals are wrong, a span exactly at the budget is
flagged as over budget, and large batches of queries are much too slow. Repair them without
changing the APIs. Only `app/prefix.py` and `app/report.py` are editable. `app/parser.py` is
trusted, working support code and must remain unchanged.

Each nonblank input line is `minute|errors`. Whitespace is stripped, blank lines are ignored,
and malformed records (wrong field count, empty minute, errors that are not a nonnegative
integer) raise ValueError.

`build_prefix(counts)` returns a list of length len(counts) + 1 whose entry i is the total of
counts[:i]. `range_total(prefix, start, end)` returns the total of the half-open span
[start, end) and raises ValueError unless 0 <= start <= end <= len(counts).
`budget_report(lines, queries, budget)` returns one dictionary per (start, end) query, in query
order: {"start", "end_exclusive", "errors", "over_budget"}. A span is over budget only when its
errors are strictly greater than the budget. A negative budget or an out-of-range span raises
ValueError. `count_over_budget(lines, queries, budget)` returns how many queried spans are over
budget. Do not mutate inputs.

Up to 30000 records and 12000 queries are assessed. An assessed full batch must finish in under
0.3 s on the runner; the whole task has a 10-second wall-clock limit. Only standard-library code
is allowed. This is a measured workload constraint, not a proof of asymptotic complexity.

Example 1:
Input: lines=["m1|2", "m2|0", "m3|5"], queries=[(0, 2), (1, 3)], budget=2
Output: [{"start": 0, "end_exclusive": 2, "errors": 2, "over_budget": false},
         {"start": 1, "end_exclusive": 3, "errors": 5, "over_budget": true}]

Example 2:
Input: build_prefix([3, 1, 4])
Output: [0, 3, 4, 8]
